title: Understanding Bias in Estimators
text: When you roll a die once, your estimate of the maximum outcome is based on just that single roll. Think about how much information you have with just one roll compared to having $$100$$ rolls. How might more data affect your estimate?

title: Exploring the Effect of More Rolls
text: Consider what happens to the range of outcomes when you roll a die $$100$$ times. Does having more rolls give you a better chance of seeing the maximum possible outcome? How does this affect the bias of your estimator?

title: Comparing Single vs. Multiple Rolls
text: If you roll a die once, your maximum outcome is limited to that single roll. With $$100$$ rolls, you have more opportunities to see higher numbers. How does this affect the bias of your estimator?
